messages.author: c796dce9bb2d010b
messages.subject: Throw or replace one chain?
parts:
Dear Stan team,

I'd like first to thank you all for the amazing work done with Stan. Special kudos for ShinyStan which is truly awesome!

I have a question I haven't been able to find an answer for. I fitted a relatively simple hierarchical model (no intercept, modeled slopes), everything went smoothly, except that obviously one of the four chains I used encountered some autocorrelation problems (see below). 

Now of course I could refit entirely the model with maybe more burnin samples. But since only one of the chains seems to have a problem, I was wondering whether there is an easy way to disgard that chain and possibly replace it with another one? Does it make sense or is there a problem with this approach I'm failing to see (I'm pretty much a n00b when it comes to serious Bayesian modeling)?

Thanks!

messages.author: a5e83218c834e013
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Throw or replace one chain?
parts: > But since only one of the chains seems to have a problem, I was wondering whether there is an easy way to disgard that chain and possibly replace it with another one?

Nope. Never. Nada.

Markov chains are valid only when they are well-behaved from any starting point
Even one chain misbehaving diagnoses pathologies that affect the others — basically
there may be a pathology region of parameter space but only one chain was lucky
enough to find it. The more chains the more likely you are to identify such pathologies,
which is why we recommend running as many chains as you can.

+1 for Michael's response.

My suggestion would be to:
- look for reparameterizations
- try more informative priors.
- higher acceptance rate, smaller stepsize


one or all of those might help the model.
